text: CNC MACHINE OPERATION AND BASIC MAINTENANCE Document ID: CNC-OPS-002 Revision: 1.0 1. Pre-Start Inspection Before starting a CNC machine, check coolant level, lubrication status, workholding, tool condition, enclosure condition, and the work offset/program selected for the job. Confirm that the workpiece is securely clamped. 2. Program Verification Verify the correct program number and revision. For a new or modified program, use the machine's approved verification procedure and confirm that tool offsets and work coordinates are appropriate. 3. Coolant Low coolant can reduce cutting performance and may cause overheating or poor chip evacuation. Refill using the approved coolant type and concentration specified by the facility. 4. Abnormal Conditions Stop the process if unusual vibration, unexpected noise, excessive heat, tool breakage, or abnormal surface finish indicates a possible fault. Do not continue cutting simply to complete the current part. 5. Daily Maintenance Remove chips using the approved cleaning method, inspect visible machine areas, check lubrication indicators, and report leaks or damaged components. Do not use compressed air in a way that can drive chips toward sensitive machine components. 6. Maintenance Records Record significant maintenance actions, alarms, replaced tooling, and observed abnormalities in the machine maintenance log.

INDUSTRIAL ROBOT WORKCELL SAFETY GUIDE Document ID: IR-SAFE-001 Revision: 1.0 1. Emergency Stop The emergency-stop circuit is intended to stop hazardous robot motion when an immediate unsafe condition is detected. After an emergency stop, the operator should identify the cause, verify that the area is safe, and follow the site's restart procedure before resuming operation. 2. Workcell Entry Before entering a robot workcell, place the robot in a safe state according to the applicable site procedure. Confirm that automatic motion cannot restart unexpectedly. Personnel should use the designated access control and follow lockout/tagout requirements where applicable. 3. Manual Operation When teaching or manually jogging a robot, operate at the permitted reduced speed and maintain awareness of the robot's reachable workspace. Keep unnecessary personnel outside the safeguarded area. 4. Restart Checks Before returning a robot to automatic operation, verify that tools and objects are clear of the robot path, guards and interlocks are in their required state, and personnel are outside the hazardous area. Follow the approved startup sequence. 5. Fault Handling If the controller reports a fault, record the fault information before resetting when practical. Do not bypass safety devices to restore production. Escalate unresolved safety-related faults to authorized maintenance personnel. 6. Preventive Maintenance Inspect cables, end-of-arm tooling, mechanical fasteners, guarding, and safety devices according to the maintenance schedule. Maintenance intervals and torque specifications should be taken from the equipment manufacturer's documentation rather than estimated by the operator.

PLC TROUBLESHOOTING AND MAINTENANCE GUIDE Document ID: PLC-MNT-003 Revision: 1.0 1. PLC Communication Failure Common symptoms of a communication problem include loss of data exchange, timeout alarms, stale status values, or a device showing an offline state. First verify power and physical network connections, then check the PLC and network diagnostics available from the control system. 2. Power Checks Before inspecting electrical hardware, follow the site's electrical safety procedure. Verify that the PLC power supply and relevant field-device power supplies are within their specified operating conditions. 3. I/O Diagnosis Compare the expected I/O state with the observed state in the PLC diagnostic or monitoring interface. A mismatch can result from field wiring, sensor/actuator issues, logic conditions, or communication problems. 4. Fault Reset A reset should not be treated as the first troubleshooting step for a recurring fault. Capture the alarm or diagnostic information, investigate the cause, and reset only according to the approved procedure. 5. Backup Keep an approved backup of PLC programs and configuration data according to site policy. Do not overwrite a working controller program with an unverified backup. 6. Escalation If a fault remains unresolved after the approved checks, escalate it to qualified controls or electrical personnel. Do not bypass interlocks or safety logic to force machine operation.
